units.sourceHTML: 2.2.1.3 Detailed Description of Context Format

units.text: The context output format starts with a two-line header, which looks like this:
units.sourceHTML: The context output format starts with a two-line header, which looks like this:

units.text: The timestamp normally looks like ‘⟦0⟧’ to indicate the date, time with fractional seconds, and time zone in ⟦1⟧Internet RFC 2822 format⟦2⟧. (The fractional seconds are omitted on hosts that do not support fractional timestamps.) However, a traditional timestamp like ‘⟦3⟧’ is used if the ⟦4⟧ locale category is either ‘⟦5⟧’ or ‘⟦6⟧’.
units.sourceHTML: The timestamp normally looks like ‘2002-02-21 23:30:39.942229878 -0800’ to indicate the date, time with fractional seconds, and time zone in Internet RFC 2822 format. (The fractional seconds are omitted on hosts that do not support fractional timestamps.) However, a traditional timestamp like ‘Thu Feb 21 23:30:39 2002’ is used if the LC_TIME locale category is either ‘C’ or ‘POSIX’.

units.text: You can change the header’s content with the ⟦0⟧ option; see ⟦1⟧Showing Alternate File Names⟦2⟧.
units.sourceHTML: You can change the header’s content with the --label=label option; see Showing Alternate File Names.

units.text: Next come one or more hunks of differences; each hunk shows one area where the files differ. Context format hunks look like this:
units.sourceHTML: Next come one or more hunks of differences; each hunk shows one area where the files differ. Context format hunks look like this:

units.text: If a hunk contains two or more lines, its line numbers look like ‘⟦0⟧’. Otherwise only its end line number appears. An empty hunk is considered to end at the line that precedes the hunk.
units.sourceHTML: If a hunk contains two or more lines, its line numbers look like ‘start,end’. Otherwise only its end line number appears. An empty hunk is considered to end at the line that precedes the hunk.

units.text: The lines of context around the lines that differ start with two space characters. The lines that differ between the two files start with one of the following indicator characters, followed by a space character:
units.sourceHTML: The lines of context around the lines that differ start with two space characters. The lines that differ between the two files start with one of the following indicator characters, followed by a space character:

units.text: A line that is part of a group of one or more lines that changed between the two files. There is a corresponding group of lines marked with ‘⟦0⟧’ in the part of this hunk for the other file.
units.sourceHTML: A line that is part of a group of one or more lines that changed between the two files. There is a corresponding group of lines marked with ‘!’ in the part of this hunk for the other file.

units.text: An “inserted” line in the second file that corresponds to nothing in the first file.
units.sourceHTML: An “inserted” line in the second file that corresponds to nothing in the first file.

units.text: A “deleted” line in the first file that corresponds to nothing in the second file.
units.sourceHTML: A “deleted” line in the first file that corresponds to nothing in the second file.

units.text: If all of the changes in a hunk are insertions, the lines of ⟦0⟧ are omitted. If all of the changes are deletions, the lines of ⟦1⟧ are omitted.
units.sourceHTML: If all of the changes in a hunk are insertions, the lines of from-file are omitted. If all of the changes are deletions, the lines of to-file are omitted.
